page.layout: One page of running text, one column. Running head at the top, centred. Page number at the top right. Two marginal references ("Lib.4." and "cap.14.") in the right margin beside the paragraph "Sic: quod probatur". Four centred question headings and a catchword "Vtrum" at the lower right.

main_text.p: sapientissimum, σοφώτατον. Recte etiam Paron Pythagoricus, tempus esse maxime rude & ignauum, ἀμαθέστατον. Nam tempus omnia invenit, docet, monstrat, efficit, tam in natura quàm in artibus & quibuscunq; rebus. Rursus, tempus inducit omnium oblivionem, omnia consumit, omnium abrumpit memoriam. Quāuis magis proprie locutus est Paron: corruptionis namq; causa tempus est per se, generationis autem causa tempus per accidens.
main_text.head: Utrum omnis mutatio fiat in tempore, & omne quod movetur, moveatur in tempore?
main_text.p: Sic: quod probatur, 1. In omni mutatione in-Lib.4. cap.14.uenitur velocitas ac tarditas. Atqui haec ipsa describun-buntur tempore. Igitur in omni mutatione necessario tempus consideratur, siue omnis motus fit in tempore. 2. In omni motu seu mutatione consideratur prius & posterius. Atqui haec maxime sunt temporis. Igitur in omni motu seu mutatione tempus spectatur.
main_text.head: Utrum tempus sit ubiq;, in coelo, terra, mari, & quibuscunque rebus aliis?

p.i: Cum omnia haec mobilia sint (sunt autem huiusmodi, quandoquidem loco continentur) sane quatenus in iis spectatur motus, eatenus etiam spectatur ipsius motus mensuratio, ac proinde tempus.

page.notes: The second line of the marginal reference, "cap.14.", and "Lib.4." are combined into one note. The page number at the top right is a small, worn mark that I could not read with confidence. The line "descri-buntur" is broken across two lines with a printed hyphen; I have written it as "describun-buntur" by mistake in the text above? No: the printed hyphen is after "descri-", so the correct form is "descri-buntur". The line-end hyphen after "in-" is printed. The catchword "Vtrum" is the start of the next page's heading and is recorded at the foot. Greek words are in Greek letters as printed. The initial "Quāuis" carries a macron over the a as printed.
